title: In the gurdwara
hookLine: no idols, no one seated higher than the Granth, heads covered for all

lines: A HALL THAT IS MOSTLY FLOOR.
cards: Shoes come off at the door, in long rows on racks. Near the entrance, in some gurdwaras, there's a basket of folded head scarves for anyone who arrived without one.
Inside, the hall is mostly floor: carpet or white sheets, and people sitting on it, cross-legged, side by side. No pews, no front row of special chairs.
At the far end, one thing is raised up, under a canopy, wrapped in cloth. Everything in the room points toward it.

teach.h: NO IDOLS; THE WORD AT THE CENTER.
teach.b: And the Guru, for Sikhs, is the Guru Granth Sahib, the word. So the code arranges the whole room around a single rule, and it shows up three ways. First: no idols.

In paraphrase, the code says no idol or image is to be set up in the gurdwara for worship. What Sikhs bow before there is the Guru Granth Sahib, the written word of the Gurus. Second: no one above the word.

teach.h: NO SEAT HIGHER THAN THE GRANTH.
teach.b: The Granth rests on a raised seat under a canopy; the congregation sits on the floor. The code says that sitting on a cushion or a special seat in the Granth's presence, in the sangat, goes against the Guru's way.

So a visiting official and the person who swept the hall that morning sit on the same floor, at the same height, facing the same way. The only raised seat in the room belongs to the word. Third: heads covered, for all.
Men and women, Sikh or visitor, cover their heads in the Granth's presence. The code also says any person, of any country, religion or caste, may come into the gurdwara.

teach.h: HEADS COVERED; THE DOOR OPEN TO ALL.
teach.b: The door is open, and what's asked is the same of everyone who walks through it: shoes off, head covered, sit down on the floor. Put the three together and the room becomes a sentence. Nothing carved stands in for God.
No person sits over anyone else. Everyone arrives in the same posture of respect.
And in the middle of it all, raised up and honored, is the word.

how: In the gurdwara, Sikhs and visitors remove their shoes, cover their heads, bow before the Guru Granth Sahib if they choose, and sit on the floor together; the Granth rests on a raised seat under a canopy.

games.why: the code says no special seat in the Granth's presence. the only raised seat belongs to the word; everyone else shares the floor.

practice: If you've been inside a gurdwara, walk through it in your mind, the shoe racks, the scarf on your head, the floor under you, the raised seat at the front; if not, use today's picture.
Then look around the room you're in now and simply notice what's raised up, and what everything points toward.

wordCard.voice: In the gurdwara. The Guru's door: no idols, no one seated higher than the Granth, and heads covered for all who enter. Today's word.

orig.note: Punjabi: the Guru's door, the place where the Guru Granth Sahib is installed.

carryVoice: Your line: no one above the word. The official and the sweeper, side by side on one floor. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Sikh Rehat Maryada, on the gurdwara (no idols; no special seat in the Granth's presence; heads covered; open to all)
